newsitem.title: INDIA: India's Rao steps down as Congress bloc's chief.
newsitem.headline: India's Rao steps down as Congress bloc's chief.

text.p: Former Indian prime minister P.V. Narasimha Rao resigned on Thursday from his last party post as chief of the Congress party's parliamentary bloc amid a flurry of corruption charges.
"I submit my resignation from the leadership of the Congress Parliamentary Party (CPP)," Rao said in his one-sentence resignation letter.

Rao, who spearheaded India's move away from socialist economic controls to open markets, led the country from 1991 until last May when the 111-year-old Congress suffered its worst defeat in a general election.
He rose to power after the assassination of former prime minister Rajiv Gandhi in May 1991.

Rao had been served an ultimatum to quit by Congress president Sitaram Kesri after parliamentary deputies passed an unprecedented resolution on Wednesday asking him to resign for the sake of party unity.
Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda's shaky ruling United Front coalition depends on Congress for crucial support.

A new leader will be elected to replace Rao on Monday, Congress party officials said. On Friday, he is scheduled to make a farewell address to the 229 members of the CPP, comprised of members of both houses of parliament.
An emergency meeting of the executive panel of Congress's parliamentary bloc expressed its deep appreciation of Rao's services both as CPP leader and prime minister.
"During his stewardship, the country was saved from serious economic crisis and provided political stability after a period of uncertainty," the panel said in a resolution.
"He provided leadership to the party and government at a traumatic hour of national life after the brutal assassination of our leader Mr Rajiv Gandhi," it added.
The 75-year-old politician has been charged in three separate corruption cases. He denies any wrongdoing in the cases which are before trial judges.
The spate of allegations forced him to step down as Congress president in September and has undercut his authority.

The campaign to drive Rao from his last position of power was part of a broader effort to revive Congress's flagging fortunes, intimately tied to Rao's wily manoeuvring during his last years in power and, more recently, his legal woes.
Political analysts fear Rao's departure could lead to a tussle among Congress heavyweights for control of the party's parliamentary bloc, giving the United Front some breathing space.
"Now that Mr Rao has resigned, creating a vacancy, I am in the race," former junior home minister Rajesh Pilot told reporters, the United News of India (UNI) said.
The Press Trust of India said another senior leader, A.R. Antulay, had urged CPP members to pick Congress president Kesri as their new chief.
"I would request members of the CPP to pass a unanimous resolution calling upon the Congress president to also shoulder the burden of the leadership of the CPP," PTI quoted him saying.
The prospect of a rejuvenated Congress has sent tremors through Deve Gowda's 13-party centre-left coalition.
The government needs the support of Congress, which controls over 142 deputies in the 545-member lower house, to survive.
Preoccupied with its own internal problems, Congress has to date been a mild critic of Deve Gowda's minority government.
